findings.title: Allowlist option read via options.get with no registration in the diff
findings.body: The allowlist comes only from options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', []). None of the eight changed files registers this key in the options defaults. Sentry's options manager raises an UnknownOption error for unregistered keys, so on a cache miss _are_all_projects_error_upsampled would raise. That call happens in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects before any dataset gating, so every events-stats request with a project could fail, not only error queries. The tests patch options in this module, so the real lookup never runs and CI would not catch it. Register the option or confirm it already exists.

findings.title: Substring match classifies negated and compound event.type filters as error queries
findings.body: The check 'event.type:error' in query is a substring test. Queries such as '!event.type:error', 'event.type:errors', or '(event.type:error OR event.type:transaction)' all return True. For those queries the count is rewritten to sum(sample_weight), but non-error rows have no sample_weight, so the sum drops them and the count is wrong (for '!event.type:error' it can come out as 0). The filter should be parsed as a token rather than matched as a substring. No test covers negation or compound queries.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) silently drops events that lack a weight
findings.body: sum() ignores NULLs, so any error event without a sample_weight contributes 0 instead of 1 to upsampled_count. This includes events ingested before the rollout and events with no client sample rate. The docstring in error_upsampling.py (lines 85-86) says no null handling is needed because the schema guarantees the column, but nothing in the diff enforces that. Time ranges spanning the rollout would silently undercount for allowlisted projects. The fallback for a missing weight should be defined explicitly, for example coalesce(sample_weight, 1).

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the request dataset, not the dataset actually queried
findings.body: The check passes the request-level dataset, but the query runs against scoped_dataset, which differs in the dashboard split path (discover for the errors-only and transactions-only sub-queries). The errors/transactions/discover guard in _should_apply_sample_weight_transform is therefore evaluated for the wrong dataset. The split path requires metrics_enhanced, so the outer dataset is always a metrics dataset there. The guard returns False and the errors-only discover sub-query is never upsampled, while the same query outside the split path would be. The decision should be made from the dataset the query actually runs on.

findings.title: Transform is not gated on metrics or on-demand routing
findings.body: The count() rewrite to upsampled_count() is applied regardless of use_metrics, has_metrics, use_metrics_layer, or on_demand_metrics_enabled, which can route a discover-dataset query to a metrics or on-demand builder. upsampled_count is registered only in discover.py's function converter, so in those routes the function would not resolve, or the query would silently fall back to a non-upsampled count. The transform should be gated on the builder actually used.

findings.title: Equations containing count() are not upsampled alongside the rewritten yAxis
findings.body: Only the exact count() entries in query_columns are rewritten. Equations passed through equations=self.get_equation_list(...) are not transformed, so an equation such as equation|count() * 2 returns un-upsampled values while the plain count() yAxis returns upsampled values in the same response. The inconsistency is not handled or documented.

findings.title: Upsampling branch in the RPC path is unreachable
findings.body: use_rpc is true only when dataset is spans_rpc or ourlogs. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False for both, so upsampling_enabled is always False when this block runs. The block is dead code, and it gives the false impression that RPC datasets get upsampled. Remove it, or rework the gating if RPC upsampling was intended.

findings.title: Allowlist check and cache write run before the dataset gate
findings.body: On every cache miss, _are_all_projects_error_upsampled runs options.get and cache.set, even for spans, metrics, and transactions queries. The dataset check on line 40 then discards the result. The cache get and set happen on every _get_event_stats call. Checking the dataset and request gate first, then returning early, would avoid the Redis round trips and the option lookup for queries that can never be upsampled.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code, so allowlist changes are only picked up after 60s
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called in the diff, and no allowlist write path invokes it. Its docstring says it should be called when the allowlist changes, but nothing does. An allowlist change therefore takes up to 60 seconds to affect upsampling, because of the cache.set at line 38. Either wire it to the option update path or remove it and correct the docstring.

findings.title: Comments claim caching and consistency that the code does not provide
findings.body: The comments say the cached result 'ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and that storing the decision 'allows for better query optimization and caching'. Nothing is cached at this point. The decision is recomputed on every _get_event_stats call, and the underlying eligibility is a 60-second cache in error_upsampling.py. Calls within one request can therefore disagree if the cache entry expires between them. The comments should be corrected.

findings.title: Unrelated change to an existing error message
findings.body: The topEvents validation message changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This has nothing to do with upsampling and is not mentioned in the PR. Any client matching the exact string will see a change. It should be split out or called out in the description.

findings.title: Bare except blocks silently ignore malformed sample rates
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps dict access and float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass'. A malformed client_sample_rate is silently dropped and the event is stored without sample_rate. This helper runs inside store_event, which many tests use, so a bad test payload gives no signal. The try around a plain dict .get chain is unnecessary. Validation should be explicit or errors should surface.

findings.title: upsampled_count is a public aggregate with a different result type from count()
findings.body: The function is registered without private=True, so users can request upsampled_count() in any discover query, including transaction queries the upsampling guard is meant to exclude. Its default_result_type is 'number' while count() is 'integer', so the field type reported in meta changes for upsampled responses. Either mark it private or document and validate the new public aggregate and its result type.

findings.title: Stray file committed at repository root
findings.body: A regular file named sentry-repo containing 'Subproject commit a5d29095...' is added at the repository root. It is not a real gitlink and appears to be an accidental artifact that pins the base commit. It should not be part of this change and should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Query-classification and cache paths are untested
findings.body: test_is_error_focused_query and test_should_apply_sample_weight_transform only check the exact strings 'event.type:error' and 'event.type:transaction'. Nothing covers negated filters ('!event.type:error'), compound queries, or 'event.type:errors', which is exactly where the substring check goes wrong. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects itself is not tested, so the cache hit and miss paths and the dataset gate are unverified. The endpoint tests also never exercise the topEvents or RPC branches where the transform is applied.
